Task: for objects 1-5 add attack cases (inputs only) that target the missed defect. Cases must remain valid inputs meeting the object's preconditions, and existing cases are never deleted. (1) AdventureWorks2025 dbo.ufnLeadingZeros: missed planted defect 'strict comparison made inclusive' (length(return_value) > 8 becomes >= 8): add input(s) whose text is exactly 8 characters (and neighbours 7 and 9 if useful). (2) WideWorldImporters Sequences.ReseedSequenceBeyondTableValues: missed 'strictly greater instead of >=': add a case where the sequence's current value equals the table's maximum boundary so > and >= differ. (3) WideWorldImporters Website.SearchForPeople: missed 'employee tested before salesperson': add a case where one person row is both employee and salesperson flagged such that testing order changes the result (read the T-SQL source in the repo to derive it). (4) WideWorldImporters Website.SearchForStockItems and (5) Website.SearchForStockItemsByTags: missed "'[..]' treated as literal characters": add cases whose search text contains square-bracket patterns that T-SQL LIKE treats as character classes (for example a bracket range matching stock item names that exist in the generated data), so literal treatment gives a different result. For each new case read the object's T-SQL and the existing case file format, give new ids following the file's scheme, label them as agent-written per the schema, and list the traps they claim, which must be present in the input.

Object 6 (Purchasing.vVendorWithAddresses): the owner chose to withdraw case A10 (AddressTypeID 9 with no matching AddressType row, outside the source foreign-key precondition). Withdraw it only by the mechanism the spec allows (see the preparation findings). Cases flagged regression:true are never deleted. If the spec allows no way, do not force it: call send_message with severity warning describing it and stop.

Objects 7 and 8 need no case-file change. Check the files parse (run `npm run adversarial -- check` using a log file redirect if the spec says check validates case files, and never concurrently with another harness process). Commit the changed *.cases.json files with explicit paths and a message listing per object the cases added or withdrawn. Final message must carry: per object the case ids added or withdrawn, the attacker stamp used, any blocker, and the commit id.
